title: California AB 2013: Generative Artificial Intelligence — Training Data Transparency Act

covered_actors: Developers of generative artificial intelligence systems or services (any person, partnership, state or local government agency, or corporation that designs, codes, produces, or substantially modifies an AI system or service for use by members of the public) released on or after January 1, 2022 and made publicly available to Californians, regardless of compensation

Exemptions apply for generative AI systems whose sole purpose is ensuring security and integrity, operating aircraft in the national airspace, or serving national security, military, or defense purposes made available solely to a federal entity

compliance_deadlines: 2026-01-01: Developers must post public website documentation of training datasets for covered generative AI systems released on or after January 1, 2022 and made publicly available to Californians (Civil Code § 3111)

Before each subsequent release or substantial modification (including retraining or fine-tuning that materially changes functionality or performance): Developers must post updated training-data documentation on their internet website (Civil Code §§ 3110(d), 3111)
policy_extraction.penalties_summary: AB 2013 adds Title 15.2 (Civil Code §§ 3110–3111) as a binding California statute but contains no express civil penalties, criminal sanctions, designated regulatory enforcement agency, or private right of action within the statutory text itself.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Enacted September 28, 2024 (Chapter 817, Statutes of 2024), adding Title 15.2 to Part 4 of Division 3 of the California Civil Code with a compliance deadline of January 1, 2026. Mandates a 12-item public website summary of training datasets—including dataset sources/owners, intended purpose alignment, data point counts and types/labels, intellectual property status, purchasing/licensing status, personal and aggregate consumer information under CCPA § 1798.140, cleaning/processing modifications, collection time windows, first-use dates, and synthetic data generation—with retrospective reach to systems released on or after January 1, 2022 and narrow carve-outs for security/integrity, national-airspace aircraft operation, and federal defense systems.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: California AB 2013 contains no legislative findings preamble, so its framing emerges directly from its operative disclosure categories in the Civil Code. Its dominant rationale aligns with fundamental rights—specifically personal-data privacy under California Consumer Privacy Act definitions, intellectual property ownership and licensing transparency, and public accountability over dataset provenance. Consumer and public safety forms a substantial secondary rationale, as the law mandates public-facing website disclosures for all generative AI systems made publicly available to Californians, requires reporting whether aggregate consumer information was used, and carves out dedicated security-and-integrity and national-airspace aviation systems to avoid disrupting operational safety functions.
